description: Record what the customer told you about their probate path and their court — the same answers as the Estate page's "Which probate route are you using?" card and the attorney task. Use it when the customer says which path they are using ("we're doing the small estate affidavit", "we're going through full probate", "we'll open ancillary probate in Florida for the condo") or what the court said about needing a lawyer ("the clerk said I need an attorney", "the court said I can file myself", "I'm working with a lawyer"). Their task list follows the answer: a no-court path or an attorney answer sets aside the do-it-yourself court steps, and an attorney answer adds what to bring the attorney. Record only what the customer said, with their words in customer_words; never decide for them which path fits the estate. get_estate_summary shows what is recorded and the path names each state offers. Records the customer's own answer. The estate's tasks follow it: a no-court path or an attorney answer moves the do-it-yourself court steps to Not Applicable and adds attorney-preparation tasks; changing the answer back restores them. An answer about a county SwiftProbate has not verified is sent to SwiftProbate staff for review.

attorney.description: Home state only: what the court told the customer about needing an attorney. 'required' = the court requires one, or they are working with one; 'self' = they can file themselves; 'unsure' = not sure yet. Leave out to keep what is recorded.

customer_words.description: Required when marking a task completed or not_applicable, or setting bypasses_probate or has_beneficiary to true: the customer's own words stating that decision, quoted exactly from their message (e.g. "mark this not required", "I paid the filing fee", "it's payable on death to my brother"). Never your own conclusion. If they haven't stated the decision, don't call — ask them.

estate_id.description: The estate to act on. Call list_my_estates first to get this id.

paths.description: The path(s) the customer says they are using in that state, by the exact names get_estate_summary lists for it, and/or "full_administration" for regular probate (or ancillary probate in another state). An empty list records "not sure yet". Leave this out to change only the attorney answer.

state_code.description: Two-letter state the answer is for. Defaults to the estate's home state. Another state only when the estate has an asset there.

name: set_probate_route
